description: Takes a picture of a character and a reference video, and generates a video of THAT character performing the motion in the reference clip - a dance, a walk, a gesture. Returns the new job's id immediately. WHEN: the user wants their character to dance, to copy a move, or to perform the motion from a clip they have. The reference clip supplies the MOVEMENT only; the character comes entirely from the picture. The reference clip must be between 3 and 30 seconds (10 if the character picture is a still portrait rather than a video reference) and reasonably large - the exact bounds are the model's, and a clip outside them is refused before anything is charged. THE CARD: this call has ALREADY put the aicut card in front of the user, and it fills in the finished media on its own. Do NOT call `show_generation` for this job - that adds a duplicate card; it is only for bringing back an EARLIER generation. HOW TO WAIT: call `wait_for_generation` with this job's id and `media` - it waits server-side and opens no card. While it answers `terminal: false`, wait `poll_after_seconds` and call it again; when `terminal: true`, tell the user in ONE short line what came out. Do not poll `get_video` / `get_image` / `get_audio` instead or spawn timers, and do NOT tell the user the generation is running in between. IF YOU CANNOT RENDER AN AICUT CARD (a terminal or plain SDK client), give the user the `url` from the wait result - aicut cannot see which clients render cards. TIMING: a video usually finishes in 1-3 minutes, and can take up to about 6. Do not assume it failed before then, and do not spawn timers or background shells to wait: call `wait_for_generation` (it waits server-side for up to 15 seconds per call), wait its `poll_after_seconds` and call it again, and stop when it answers `terminal: true`. `get_video` is a single immediate read for one job's raw fields - it is not the waiting loop and must not be polled in one. COST: this spends the user's tokens, and the price is the reference clip's LENGTH times a per-second rate that depends on the model and the resolution - so a 30-second reference costs ten times a 3-second one. The clip's length is MEASURED BY THE SERVER from the file itself, never taken from anything you say - that measurement is the price and the charge. A clip aicut cannot measure (a WebM, or a file whose header it cannot read) is REFUSED with nothing charged; re-encode it to MP4 and try again. There is deliberately no length argument on this tool. Pass `estimate_only: true` first to get the exact price. An EXTERNAL url is downloaded and stored on the account before it can be measured, which uses one of the account's daily media-ingest slots. Quoting and then creating from the SAME url costs that once, not twice - aicut reuses what it already imported - and a url already on the account costs nothing at all. SPENDS TOKENS: quote it first (`estimate_only: true`), state the price IN THE SAME MESSAGE as your ask, and wait for a go that names THIS purchase - a bare 'yes' counts only as the direct answer to that priced ask, and an ambiguous one means ask again. The full SPENDING RULES in this server's instructions apply here. IF THE USER REPORTS A CHARGE OR STEP THEY DID NOT EXPECT: re-read your own tool calls and say which you made; aicut cards cannot spend (full rule in this server's instructions). IDEMPOTENCY: `idempotency_key` is optional. Reusing a key REPLAYS the job it first created (even with different settings), so never reuse one to make another generation; the full rules are in this server's instructions (IDEMPOTENCY). OUTPUT: JSON for you to read. Tell the user the media URL plus a one-line summary; do not paste raw JSON, job ids or internal field names.

character_image.description: URL of the picture of the character to animate. Either a URL an earlier generation or upload on THIS account returned, or a genuinely external public https URL - aicut downloads it, size-caps it and stores it on the account first. An aicut-hosted URL belonging to a DIFFERENT account is refused.

character_orientation.description: What the character picture is: `video` (the default) for a full-body or moving subject, `image` for a still portrait - which also lowers the reference clip's maximum length to 10 seconds.

estimate_only.description: Price these exact settings and create nothing. Returns the token cost, the account balance, and whether the balance covers it. Costs nothing and changes nothing.

idempotency_key.description: Optional retry-safety key. Read the IDEMPOTENCY note in this tool's description before using one - a reused key returns the first job instead of making a new one.

model.description: Which motion-control model to use. `kling-3.0-motion-control` is the better and much more expensive one (about 4x); `kling-2.6-motion-control` is the everyday choice. Ask the user rather than picking the expensive one for them.

reference_video.description: URL of the video whose motion should be copied. Either a URL an earlier generation or upload on THIS account returned, or a genuinely external public https URL - aicut downloads it, size-caps it and stores it on the account first. An aicut-hosted URL belonging to a DIFFERENT account is refused.

resolution.description: Output resolution. 1080p costs more per second. Never set this to save the user tokens or to make a generation cheaper - set it only when the user explicitly asked for this value, and never carry it over from an earlier request.

name: motion_control
title: Make a character copy a video's motion
